name: Lendf.Me (imBTC ERC-777 reentrancy)
summary: MoneyMarket.supply() credited the supplier only after doTransferIn(), so imBTC's ERC-777 tokensToSend hook re-entered withdraw() while the deposit was still counted, letting the attacker keep both the collateral credit and the withdrawn tokens.

loss.notes: dForce reports that approximately $25 million of cryptoassets were drained from Lendf.Me across the coherent exploit campaign. Nearly all assets were later recovered and redistributed; this measurement records gross assets lost at exploit time rather than the post-recovery net outcome.

ageReset.description: The defect-bearing MoneyMarket runtime was created directly in this transaction and remained unchanged through the exploit.

sources.note: Reviewed the selected exploit receipt and call trace, MoneyMarket creation transaction and bytecode, historical runtime, disassembly, commit-pinned reproduction, PeckShield's technical analysis, and dForce's official resolution report. The trace calls MoneyMarket 0x0eee3e3828a45f7601d5f54bf49bb01d1a9df5ea directly: supply() invokes imBTC.transferFrom(), imBTC's ERC-777 tokensToSend callback re-enters MoneyMarket.withdraw() before the outer supply updates accounting, and the outer call then credits the deposit again. MoneyMarket is a direct 19,206-byte deployment with no DELEGATECALL, SELFDESTRUCT, or CREATE2 opcode. Its runtime hash is 0x01742f4a4c5582771d36e79e1aa009070116bd33c232e42321d03c6ab1314c89 both at deployment block 8295432 and immediately before exploit block 9899738, establishing 22,185,718 seconds of unchanged code. dForce reports approximately $25 million drained across the campaign and later recovered nearly in full.

limitations: The $25 million loss is dForce's rounded campaign-level report and is not expanded into exact per-asset components here.
Subsequent asset recovery is excluded from the exploit-time gross-loss measurement.
